dedupe_keys.name: caravan global community dataset of streamflow meteorological forcing and catchment attributes 6 830 catchments

description: Caravan is an open, global community dataset for large-sample hydrology that standardises and aggregates existing CAMELS-style catchment datasets, together with open-source code to extend it to new basins. It was introduced by Frederik Kratzert, Grey Nearing, Nans Addor and co-authors as a Data Descriptor in Scientific Data in 2023, and the GitHub repository serves as its code base and community hub. Coverage: at release, meteorological forcing, streamflow and static catchment attributes (geophysical, sociological and climatological) for 6,830 catchments from seven existing large-sample datasets, derived with the same variables and procedures everywhere; community extensions add further regions, and the MultiMet extension adds nowcasts (CPC, IMERG, CHIRPS), forecasts (ECMWF IFS HRES, GraphCast, CHIRPS-GEFS) and ERA5-Land for all basins. Format and access: two Zenodo records, one in netCDF and one in CSV (since version 1.6), MultiMet data as zarr on Zenodo and a public Google Cloud bucket, and Google Earth Engine code to derive forcing and attributes for new catchments; free. Licence: data under open licences (the paper states all data are public with an open licence and is itself CC-BY-4.0); code BSD-3-Clause. Caveats: original Caravan data are in local time while MultiMet is in UTC, streamflow quality depends on each source dataset, and extensions vary in coverage; the Zenodo pages were not read. Simulation uses: training and benchmarking rainfall-runoff and flood forecasting models that feed hazard exposure, reservoir capacity planning and climate adaptation of water infrastructure. Related records: GRDC (data-grdc-global-runoff-database) is a global discharge archive, and Google's Flood Forecasting API (data-google-flood-hub-flood-forecasting-api) serves forecasts from models of this kind. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo dataset); code BSD-3-Clause.
